full_text:
**Verdict: KNOWN.** Confidence is medium-high.

**1. Model family.** This is a classical frustrated Heisenberg J1–J2–J3 model on the square lattice. It has a ring-degenerate minimum in reciprocal space, so it is a spiral spin liquid (SSL). The family sits in statistical physics and frustrated magnetism. Your couplings follow the J3 = J2/2 line, which gives the ring.

**2. The specific behaviour.** The behaviours you list are all described in the literature:

- **Intermediate-temperature SSL and the ordering transition.**
  - The SSL has a continuous contour of wave vectors in reciprocal space, and phase transitions along the ring-minimum line separate disordered SSL states from low-temperature ordered states that break lattice-rotational symmetry.
  - The same family of ideas covers spiral order by disorder, in which discrete lattice rotation symmetry stays broken as a thermal nematic. That result is for the honeycomb J1–J2 model.
- **Defects of the local wave-vector field.**
  - Yan and Reuther's "Low-energy structure of spiral spin liquids" (Phys. Rev. Research 4, 023175, 2022) finds a second type of topological defect, vortices in the local momentum vector field on the coarse-grained lattice, besides the usual spin vortices.
  - It is done for the XY model with Monte Carlo, on 400×400 lattices.
  - I took the authors from a later citation ("Yan and Reuther^15") and not from the abstract page.
- **Half-wound defects with a spin-frame rotation.** This is the closest match to your observations. Glittum, Yan and Reuther, "Fractional vortices in a spin-isotropic spiral spin liquid" (arXiv:2609.15941, 2026; data at Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.23390512), makes these claims:
  - The elementary defects of a spin-isotropic Heisenberg SSL are half-vortices. Each carries a π winding of the spiral wave vector together with a π rotation of the spin frame.
  - Large-scale Monte Carlo on a square-lattice model shows these half-vortices are dense in the SSL regime and bind tightly below an order-by-disorder transition.
  - They are classified by the order-parameter space [U(1)×SO(3)]/ℤ₂, in which reversing the wave vector is equivalent to reversing the spiral-plane normal.
  - The summary also mentions a family of vortex types with concerted windings of spin direction, plane normal and wave vector. The simulations use 200×200 lattices.
  - This matches your observations: a wave-vector winding of 0.5 turns (π) for the commonest defect, a rarer class that winds only the spin frame, dense defects in the correlated regime, and a lattice-rotation-breaking transition at low T.

**Review and context sources.**
- Niggemann et al., "Classical spiral spin liquids as a possible route to quantum spin liquids" (J. Phys.: Condens. Matter, IOPscience 10.1088/1361-648X/ab4480). It builds a Heisenberg SSL model on the square lattice with J1, J2 and J3. I only saw the title and abstract, so I can't confirm the author list or year from the search.
- Gonzalez, Fancelli, Yan and Reuther, "Magnetic properties of the spiral spin liquid and surrounding phases in the square lattice XY model" (Phys. Rev. B 110, 085106). This is the XY-model phase-diagram companion paper.
- The IOPscience article "The finite-temperature behavior of a triangular Heisenberg antiferromagnet" covers the thermal behaviour of a Heisenberg SSL, but on the triangular lattice.

**Caveats.**
- I could only read a summary of the 2026 preprint (a Pith review page) and not the full text. I did not confirm the exact couplings (J1 = −1, J2 = 0.28, J3 = 0.14), the 0.66 ring radius, or the numbers 0.03, 0.003, 0.0268 and 0.19.
- I am therefore treating the preprint as an equivalent system because the model type, lattice size, defect type and transition all match. If those couplings are exactly its model, this is KNOWN. If they differ only in parameters, it is a trivial variant.
- The preprint is recent (about 48 days old at search time) and may not be peer reviewed.
- The earliest clear source for wave-vector defects is Yan and Reuther 2022, for the XY model. The earliest source for the Heisenberg half-vortex classification is the 2026 preprint.
